questions.question: Assertion (A): Rest (of a body) is a relative term. Reason (R): Motion of a body may be absolute term.
options: Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is true; Reason (R) is a correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is true; Reason (R) is not a correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Assertion (A): “Rest (of a body) is a relative term.” This is true; rest must always be described relative to some observer or frame of reference. Reason (R): “Motion of a body may be an absolute term.” This is false, because motion is also relative. There is no absolute frame of reference in classical mechanics. Hence, the assertion is true while the reason is false.

questions.question: The ratio of displacement to distance is
questions.explanation: Displacement is the shortest distance between two points, while distance is the actual path length. So, DisplacementDistance≤1{{Displacement}}{{Distance}} 1 The ratio: Is 1 in straight-line motion without change in direction. Is less than 1 when path is not straight or involves reversal. Correct option: D (May be 1) Explanation:The ratio depends on the nature of motion. It may be 1, but not always.

questions.question: The numerical ratio of displacement to the distance covered is always:
options: Equal to or less than one
Equal to or greater than one
questions.explanation: Displacement≤Distance⇒DisplacementDistance≤1{Displacement} {Distance} {{Displacement}}{{Distance}} 1 The ratio is: Exactly 1 for straight-line motion without change in direction. Less than 1 when the path is curved or involves turning back. Correct option: C Explanation:Displacement is the shortest distance between initial and final positions, while distance is the total path length. Hence, the ratio is always ≤ 1.

questions.question: An aeroplane flies 400 {~m} north and 300 {~m} south and then flies 1200 {~m} upwards then net displacement is
questions.explanation: Given: Northward: +400 m+400 \, {m} Southward: –300 m–300 \, {m} Upward: +1200 m+1200 \, {m} Net horizontal displacement (north-south): 400−300=100 m (north)400 - 300 = 100 \, {m (north)} Net vertical displacement: 1200 m (up)1200 \, {m (up)} Net displacement (3D vector): Displacement=1002+12002=10000+1440000=1450000=1204.16 m{Displacement} = √(100² + 1200² = √{10000 + 1440000) = √(1450000) = 1204.16 \, {m} ≈ 1204 m Correct option: A (1204 m)

questions.question: A person moves on a semicircular track of radius 40 {m} . If he starts at one end of the track and reaches the other end, find the magnitude of displacement of the person.
questions.explanation: The person moves along a semicircular track of radius = 40 m. Displacement is the straight-line distance between the start and end points, which are ends of the diameter. So, Displacement=Diameter=2×radius=2×40=80 m{Displacement} = {Diameter} = 2 {radius} = 2 40 = 80 \, {m}

questions.question: A man goes 10 {~m} towards North, then 20 {~m} towards east then displacement is
questions.explanation: Given: Northward = 10 m Eastward = 20 m Displacement = diagonal of right triangle: Displacement=102+202=100+400=500=22.36 m{Displacement} = √(10² + 20² = √{100 + 400) = √(500) = 22.36 \, {m} ≈ 22.5 m Correct option: A (22.5 m)

questions.question: A hall has the dimensions 10 {~m} 10 {~m} 10 {~m} . {A} fly starting at one corner ends up at a diagonally opposite corner. The magnitude of its displacement is nearly
questions.explanation: Concept Used: To find the displacement from one corner of a cubical hall (10 m × 10 m × 10 m) to its diagonally opposite corner, use the 3D diagonal formula: Displacement=l²+b²+h²{Displacement} = √(l² + b² + h² Given: l=b=h=10 ml = b = h = 10 \, {m) ⇒Displacement=102+102+102=300=103 m {Displacement} = √(10² + 10² + 10² = √{300) = 10√(3) \, {m} Final Answer: 2. 103 m10√(3) \, {m}

questions.question: A particle moves along a circular path of radius r . The distance and displacement of the particle after one complete revolution are respectively :
questions.explanation: Given: Circular path of radius rr One complete revolution Distance: Distance=Circumference=2πr{Distance} = {Circumference} = 2π r Displacement: After a full circle, particle returns to the starting point → Displacement=0{Displacement} = 0 Correct option: B (2πr, 0) Explanation: Distance is total path length around the circle Displacement is the shortest distance between initial and final points — zero for full revolution.

questions.question: A body is moving along the circumference of a circle of radius ' R ' and completes 34th of the revolution. then the ratio of its displacement to distance is.
questions.explanation: Distance travelled when the particle covers 3434 of a full circle is distance  =  34×circumference  =  34×2πR  =  3πR2.{distance} \;=\; 34 {circumference} \;=\; 34 2π R \;=\; {3π R}{2}. Displacement is the straight‐line chord joining the starting and ending points after 3434 revolution (i.e.\ an arc of 270∘270^). The chord length for an arc of angle θ is 2Rsin⁡ ⁣(θ2)2R\!(2). Here, θ=3π2={3π}{2}, so displacement  =  2R sin⁡ ⁣(3π2×12)=  2R sin⁡ ⁣(3π4)=  2R×22=  R 2.{displacement} \;=\; 2R\,\!({3π}{2}12) =\; 2R\,\!({3π}{4}) =\; 2R √2/2 =\; R\,√2. Hence, the ratio of displacement to distance is  R 2 3πR2=  2 2 3π   =  8 3π .\,R\,√2\,/{3π R{2}} =\; 2\,√2/\,3π\, \;=\; {√(8)}{\,3π\,}.

questions.question: A boy completes one round of a circular track of radius 20 {~m} in 50 seconds. The displacement at the end of 4 minute 10 second will be
questions.explanation: Given: Radius r=20 mr = 20 \, {m} Time per round = 50 s Total time = 4 min 10 s=250 s4 \, {min} \, 10 \, {s} = 250 \, {s} Number of rounds completed: 25050=5 rounds250/50 = 5 \, {rounds} In circular motion, displacement after full rounds is zero, because the boy returns to the starting point. Correct option: D (Zero)

questions.question: A particle is moving along a circle such that it completes one revolution in 40 seconds. In 2 minutes 20 seconds, the ratio { { |displacement| }}{ { distance }} is
questions.explanation: Given: Time for 1 revolution = 40 s Total time = 2 min 20 s = 140 s Number of revolutions: 14040=3.5 revolutions140/40 = 3.5 \, {revolutions} Distance: Each revolution = circumference = 2πr2π rSo: Distance∝3.5×(2πr){Distance} 3.5 (2π r) Displacement: After 3 full revolutions → returns to starting point.Then covers half revolution → ends up on diametrically opposite side So: Displacement=diameter=2r{Displacement} = {diameter} = 2r Ratio: DisplacementDistance=2r3.5⋅2πr=13.5π=111{{Displacement}}{{Distance}} = 2r/3.5 2π r = 1/3.5π = 1/11

questions.question: Given below are some statements regarding distance and displacement. I. Distance is always greater than displacement. II. Distance can be equal to displacement. III. Displacement can be zero. Which one of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Distance is the length of the path covered to reach from initial to final positions and displacement is the shortest distance between the initial and the final positions. So, distance is greater than or equal to displacement.Yes, Displacement can be zero. For example- When a person moves from an initial point and comes back to the initial point, his displacement will be zero. So statement II, III are correct.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: Displacement may be equal to the distance covered. Reason R: For a body moving in a circle, direction of velocity is expressed by tangent drawn at that point.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.explanation: If a body moves in a straight line, then displacement = distance otherwise displacement < distance, hence Assertion is true. When a body moves in a circle, the direction of instantaneous velocity is shown by tangent drawn at that point. But both A and R are not relevant to each other.

questions.question: Assertion: Speed can't be negative, but velocity can be negative.Reason: Distance can't be negative but displacement can be negative.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is not a correct explanation of the Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false and Reason is true
questions.explanation: Because speed is the magnitude of velocity (and hence derived from distance, which has no sign), it can never be negative. Velocity, however, depends on displacement, which can be positive or negative in one‐dimensional motion. Thus, both statements are correct, and the Reason does correctly explain the Assertion.

questions.question: An object is located at any point O at t=0 {~s} . From t=0 {~s} to t=5 {~s} , it continuously changes its position and reaches point P . In the next 5 {~s} , it does not change its position. For the above situation, which of the following statement is/are correct? I. The object is in motion from point O to point P . II. The object is at rest from t=5 {~s} to t=10 {~s} . III. The object is in motion from t=0 {~s} to t=10 {~s} .
questions.explanation: From the description: Between t=0t=0 s and t=5t=5 s, the object moves from OO to PP (so it is in motion then). Between t=5t=5 s and t=10t=10 s, it remains at the same position (so it is at rest). Checking the statements: (I) “The object is in motion from OO to PP.”True for 0≤t≤50 t 5. (II) “The object is at rest from t=5t=5 s to t=10t=10 s.”True because its position does not change in that interval. (III) “The object is in motion from t=0t=0 s to t=10t=10 s.”Not true, since it is at rest from t=5t=5 to t=10t=10. Hence, the correct statements are (I) and (II).

Correct option: D (Zero)

questions.question: A car moves with speed 60 {~km} / {h} for 1 hour in east direction and with same speed for 30 {~min} in south direction. The displacement of car from initial position is
questions.explanation: Given: Speed = 60 km/h60 \, {km/h} 1 hour east → distance = 60 km60 \, {km} 30 min south → distance = 60×12=30 km60 1/2 = 30 \, {km} Displacement (vector from start to end): Displacement=602+302=3600+900=4500=305 km{Displacement} = √(60² + 30² = √{3600 + 900) = √(4500) = 30√(5) \, {km} Correct option: C (30√5 km) Explanation:Displacement is diagonal of the right triangle formed by two perpendicular motions.

questions.question: A body is moving along a straight line path with constant velocity. At an instant of time the distance travelled by it is {S} and its displacement is D . then
questions.explanation: Given: A body is moving along a straight line with constant velocity. Distance travelled = SS Displacement = DD From NCERT Physics:For motion along a straight line with constant velocity, the path does not curve or change direction. Therefore: Displacement D=Distance S{Displacement } D = {Distance } S Correct option: A Explanation:In rectilinear motion with constant velocity (i.e., without changing direction), the magnitude of displacement is equal to the total distance travelled.

questions.question: A car travels a distance d on a straight road in two hours and then returns to the starting point in next three hours. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Given: Distance one way = dd Time to go = 2 hours Time to return = 3 hours Total distance = d+d=2dd + d = 2d Total time = 2+3=52 + 3 = 5 hours Average speed: Average speed=Total distanceTotal time=2d5{Average speed} = {{Total distance}}{{Total time}} = 2d/5 Correct option: B 2d52d/5 Explanation:Average speed is total path length divided by total time, regardless of varying speeds.

questions.question: A particle moves along {x} -axis with speed 6 {~m} / {s} for the first half distance of a journey and the second half distance with a speed 3 {~m} / {s} . The average speed in the total journey is
questions.explanation: Given: First half distance @ 6 m/s Second half distance @ 3 m/s Let total distance = 2d2dThen: Time for first half =d6= d/6 Time for second half =d3= d/3 Total time: d6+d3=d+2d6=3d6=d2d/6 + d/3 = d + 2d/6 = 3d/6 = d/2 Average speed: =Total distanceTotal time=2dd2=4 m/s= {{Total distance}}{{Total time}} = 2d/{d{2}} = 4 \, {m/s} Correct option: C (4 m/s) Note: When equal distances are covered at different speeds v1,v2v_1, v_2,average speed = 2v1v2v1+v2=2⋅6⋅36+3=42v_1v_2/v_1 + v_2 = 2 6 3/6 + 3 = 4 m/s.

questions.question: A person travels along a straight road for the first t/3 time with a speed v_{1} and for next 2 t/3 time with a speed v_{2} . Then the mean speed v is given by
questions.explanation: Time segments: First t3{t}{3} with speed v1.v_1. Next 2t3{2t}{3} with speed v2.v_2. Distances: d1=v1 ⁣(t3),d2=v2 ⁣(2t3). d_1 = v_1\!({t}{3}), d_2 = v_2\!({2t}{3}). Total distance d=d1+d2d = d_1 + d_2. Total time =t.=t. Therefore, the mean (average) speed vv is v = d1+d2 t  = v1 t3+v2 2t3t = v13+2 v23 = v1+2 v23.v \,=\,d_1 + d_2/\,t\, \,=\,v_1\,{t/3 + v_2\,{2t}{3}}{t} \,=\,v_1/3 + 2\,v_2/3 \,=\,v_1+2\,v_2/3.

questions.question: A car travels a distance of 2000 {~m} . If the first half distance is covered at 40 {~km} / hour and the second half at velocity v and if the average velocity is 48 {km} / hour, then the value of v is
questions.explanation: Concept Used: This is a different-speed-for-equal-distances problem.When a journey is divided into equal distances with different speeds, the average speed is given by: vavg=2v1v2v1+v2v_{{avg}} = 2 v_1 v_2/v_1 + v_2 Given: vavg=48 km/hv_{{avg}} = 48 \, {km/h} v1=40 km/hv_1 = 40 \, {km/h} v2=vv_2 = v (to be found) Apply the formula: 48=2×40×v40+v48 = 2 40 v/40 + v Cross-multiply: 48(40+v)=80v⇒1920+48v=80v⇒1920=32v⇒v=192032=6048(40 + v) = 80v 1920 + 48v = 80v 1920 = 32v v = 1920/32 = 60 🔹 Final Answer: B. 60 km/h60 \, {km/h}

questions.question: A car runs at constant speed on a circular track of radius 100 {~m} taking 62.8 {~s} on each lap. What is the average speed and average velocity on each complete lap?
questions.explanation: Given:Radius r=100 mr = 100 \, {m},Time for one lap t=62.8 st = 62.8 \, {s} Circumference =2πr=2×π×100=628 m= 2π r = 2 π 100 = 628 \, {m} Average speed: Average speed=Total distanceTotal time=62862.8=10 m/s{Average speed} = {{Total distance}}{{Total time}} = 628/62.8 = 10 \, {m/s} Average velocity:Since displacement over a full lap is zero (returns to starting point), Average velocity=0{Average velocity} = 0 Correct option: B Explanation:In a circular path, though speed is constant, average velocity over a complete lap is zero due to zero net displacement.

questions.question: An object moves with a constant speed of 20 {~m} / {s} . What is the displacement after 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: For uniform motion, displacement s= speed time. s=20 5=100 {~m}

questions.question: If the distance S covered by a moving car in rectilinear motion with a speed v in time t is given by S = vt, then the car undergoes;
questions.explanation: The given relation S=v tS = v\,t directly tells us that the car travels distance SS at a constant speed vv. Since vv is constant, the motion has zero acceleration and hence is a uniform‐velocity motion.

questions.question: The position (x) of a particle at any time t is given by the equation x=bt, where b is a positive constant. Which of the following option given below is correct ?
questions.explanation: x= btVelocity, v=dxdt=bAccleration, a=dvdt=0 Hence, Velocity is constant, and accleration is zero.

questions.question: If for a particle position x ∝ t², then:
questions.explanation: Given:x∝t²⇒x=kt²x t² x = kt², where kk is a constant. Velocity: v=dxdt=ddt(kt²)=2ktv = dx/dt = d/dt(kt²) = 2kt Acceleration: a=dvdt=ddt(2kt)=2ka = dv/dt = d/dt(2kt) = 2k So, acceleration is constant. Explanation:Differentiating position x=kt²x = kt² twice shows that the particle has linearly increasing velocity and constant acceleration.

questions.explanation: Given s(t)=2t²+2t−4.s(t) = 2t² + 2t - 4. Differentiate once w.r.t. tt to get the velocity: v(t)=dsdt=4t+2.v(t) = ds/dt = 4t + 2. Differentiate again to get the acceleration: a(t)=d²sdt²=4.a(t) = d²s/dt² = 4. Thus, the particle’s acceleration is 4 m/s24\,{m/s}².

questions.question: If displacement (x) of a particle is given as x=3t²-4 (m); Find nature of its acceleration at t = 1 sec.
questions.explanation: V=dxdt=ddt3t²-4=6t m/s a=dvdt=ddt6t=6 m/s² Since acceleration does not depend upon time, so it is constant (uniform).

questions.question: The displacement of particle is given by x=a0+a1t2−a2t²3 What is its acceleration?

Differentiate again to get the acceleration: a  =  dvdt  =  −  2 a23.a \;=\;dv/dt \;=\;-\;2\,a_2/3. Hence, the acceleration is −2 a23.-2\,a_2/3.

questions.explanation: {aligned} & x=a_0-a_1 t+a_2 t² \\ & d x/d t=-a_1+2 a_2 t \\ & d² x/d t²=2 a_2{aligned}

questions.question: Which one of the following equations represent the motion of a body with finite constant acceleration. In these equations y denotes the position of the body at time t and a, b and c are the constant of the motion -
questions.explanation: For constant acceleration: The equation of motion is: y=ut+12at²y = ut + 1/2at² This is a quadratic equation in time. Among the given options, only Option C matches this form: y=at+bt²y = at + bt² (Here, aa is initial velocity, b=12ab = 1/2a) Correct option: C Explanation:Position–time relation for constant acceleration is a second-degree polynomial in time.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is correct for retardation?
options: May be +ve and -ve acceleration is called retardation
Acceleration which is in the direction of motion
Acceleration which is parallel to the velocity.
questions.explanation: (2) Retardation refers to an acceleration opposite to the direction of the velocity (i.e., it reduces the body’s speed). Whether that acceleration is numerically “positive” or “negative” depends on one’s choice of coordinate axes. For instance: If an object is moving in the +x+x direction, then an acceleration in the −x-x direction is a retardation (and will appear “negative”). If an object is moving in the −x-x direction, then an acceleration in the +x+x direction is a retardation (and will appear “positive”). Thus, the sign of the acceleration alone is not what defines retardation; rather, it is acceleration opposing the velocity. Therefore, from the given choices, the statement that it “may be +ve or -ve acceleration” most correctly describes retardation.

Time to come to rest means v(t)=0v(t)=0, so 12−3t²=0  ⟹  t²=4  ⟹  t=2 s(taking t>0).12 - 3t²=0 \;\;t²=4 \;\;t=2\,{s}({taking }t>0). Positions at t=0t=0 and t=2t=2: x(0)=40,x(2)=40+12(2)  −  (2)3=40+24−8=56.x(0)=40, x(2)=40+12(2)\;-\;(2)³=40+24-8=56. Hence the particle travels 56−40=16 m56-40=16\,{m} before coming to rest. questions.question: A balloon starts rising from ground with an acceleration of 1.25 {~m} / {sec}² . After 8 seconds a stone is released from the balloon. The maximum height from the ground reached by stone will be
questions.explanation: A particle that breaks away from a moving body keeps its speed but loses its acceleration. When the balloon is released, it is at height s above the ground and having upward velocity u. s=12×(1.25)×64=40 m u=1.25×8=10m/sec Because of the stone's movement from the balloon to the highest point, u=10msec a=−g=−10m/sec² v=0, using v²−u²=2as 0-100 = -2 x 10 x s s = 5 metres. Hence, maximum height from ground = 40+5 = 45 m.
